title: Embed chat presentation and turn replay through shared packages
description:
As an application developer, I want to consume Chatticus chat presentation and turn-stream handling as dependencies so that embedded chat shares one implementation.

Feature: Embed shared Chatticus chat
  Scenario: Render and send in another application
    Given a standalone application supplies messages, state and send callbacks
    When its editor sends a message through the shared chat surface
    Then the host receives the message once
    And the surface renders host-supplied messages without Chatticus login, roster or computer state
  Scenario: Replay one observed turn
    Given a transport disconnects after a stored event
    When the shared client reconnects
    Then it requests events after the last seen sequence
    And duplicate sequences are not delivered twice
  Scenario: Preserve the Chatticus application
    Given the product consumes its shared chat dependencies
    When a member reads or sends a message
    Then its existing chat and activity behavior remains available

Links: Papyrus PPY-a438d0 and PPY-7962e3. Server Python migration is a later independent phase. No deployment or package publication in this task.

comments.text: Implementation paused at user request. Planning is filed in docs/papyrus-chat-integration-handoff.md and the Papyrus docs/PPY-eeb023-chatticus-chat-plan branch. No production code was changed. UI/client extraction is independent of server language; later server work should reuse existing TypeScript Pi Durable, not assume a Python migration. Coordinate papyrus-console-shell changes with the loading UX owner. No merge, package publication, deployment or security-access changes are authorized. Planning records remain open on a non-deploying handoff branch because pushing develop would trigger deployments.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implementation resumed on BlackbookM1 after user direction. Feature branch feature/chatticus-080b0e-shared-chat extends the existing root UI-kit exports with chat-client, chat-react and scoped styles; Papyrus will pin the implementation commit. No Python migration, workers, registry publication, merge or deployment. Preserve planning records here; product changes remain in the separate feature branch. Initial standalone-consumer and replay Gherkin scenarios fail because the public chat exports do not yet exist.
